title: Fibra Next Raises $431 Million; Largest Mexico IPO in Years
content: Mexican real estate investment trust Fibra Next raised 8 billion pesos ($431 million) through its initial public offering, the country’s biggest stock debut in seven years.

title: Stocks Rally on Trade Deal Hopes, Dollar Falls: Markets Wrap
content: Asian equities rose in their longest winning streak since January, as stock bulls drew fresh conviction from signs the US may strike more trade deals after clinching a pact with Japan.

title: Fortescue Hits Iron Ore Record, Drops More Hydrogen Projects
content: Fortescue Ltd. shipped a record amount of iron ore last quarter — waving away concerns of diminishing demand from China, the world’s biggest buyer of the steel-making ingredient — and said it would drop several green-energy projects.

title: Todd Boehly-Backed Accelerant, Holders Raise $724 Million in IPO
content: Accelerant Holdings and some of its backers raised $724 million in an upsized US initial public offering priced above the marketed range, the latest insurance-related listing to meet with strong demand.

title: Gold Slips as Haven Demand Eases on US Trade Deals Optimism
content: Gold extended a decline as progress in talks between the US and key trading partners hurt demand for haven assets.

title: Tesla Has Talent But Needs Stability: Westly (Correct)
content: Steve Westly, Founder and Managing Partner, The Westly Group, and Former Tesla Executive, says Tesla needs to get its top executives in place and new products to market. title: Education Tech Firm McGraw Hill Raises $414.6 Million in IPO
content: McGraw Hill Inc. raised $414.6 million in its US initial public offering, pricing shares of the education company below its marketed range.

title: Oil Steadies With US Trade Tariff Outlook, Stockpiles in Focus
content: Oil steadied after a string of losses, with investors looking to US trade talk progress and low inventory levels.

title: JPMorgan, BofA Leaders Subpoenaed by US Lawmakers Over CATL IPO
content: JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Bank of America Corp. were subpoenaed by US lawmakers over their role in the initial public offering of Chinese battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd.

title: EU Wrestles With China’s Chokehold Over Crucial Defense Supplies
content: European metals traders are engaged in an increasingly frantic scramble to secure rare-earth metal supplies after it became all but impossible to directly source them from China.

title: China State Fund Pumped $28 Billion Into ETFs as Turmoil Raged
content: Chinese sovereign wealth fund Central Huijin Investment Ltd. pumped around 197.5 billion yuan ($27.6 billion) into exchange-traded funds in the second quarter, pushing back against a stock market rout that followed US President Donald Trump’s tariff announcements.

title: Capital Inflows Spark Hunt for Value in Singapore’s Stock Market
content: Singapore’s S$5 billion ($3.9 billion) push to revive its stock market is prompting investors to look beyond pricey bank shares and find value in overlooked sectors as capital starts flowing in.

title: New Fortress Energy Taps Houlihan for Advice Amid Bond Rout
content: Billionaire investor Wes Edens’ New Fortress Energy Inc. has tapped Houlihan Lokey for advice in anticipation of talks with creditors to cut its debt load, according to people with knowledge of the situation who asked not to be identified because they’re not authorized to speak publicly.

title: Surprise Trade Deal for Japan Turns Stock Losers Into Winners
content: The unexpected US-Japan trade deal announced Wednesday may end up being a tipping point for the fortunes of many sectors in the stock market — with losers turning into winners, and vice versa.

title: ‘Bullish Outlook Is There’: Franklin Templeton’s Dudley
content: Franklin Templeton Senior Investment Strategist Katrina Dudley says good economic momentum supports stock market broadening and the market’s resilience in face of bad news gives us confidence. She speaks with Vonnie Quinn and Scarlet Fu on “The Close.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Blackstone Gathers $5 Billion for Secondhand Infrastructure Bets
content: Blackstone Inc. has gathered about $5 billion for its latest fund designed to make secondhand bets on infrastructure, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Southern CEO Warns of ‘Revolution’ If Power Bills Aren’t Cheaper
content: The chief of utility giant Southern Co. warned that Americans will revolt if they end up on the hook for the soaring power costs associated with AI demand.

title: Ardagh Creditors to Pay Owner Paul Coulson Up to $300 Million to Walk Away
content: Ardagh Group SA creditors are set to pay billionaire owner Paul Coulson as much as $300 million as part of a deal to hand over the keys to the company, according to people with knowledge of the situation.

title: Chevron to Cut More than 600 Jobs in $53 Billion Hess Deal
content: Chevron Corp. is cutting almost 650 jobs in the Houston area and North Dakota after completing the $53 billion takeover of Hess Corp.

title: SEC Hits Pause on Bitwise ETF Offering Broad Crypto Exposure
content: A key US regulator halted the approval process for a new cryptocurrency exchange-traded fund just hours after initially signing off, in a setback for digital-asset proponents hoping for easy-to-trade funds that expand access to more tokens.

title: 'No One Wants to Buy Elon's Products,' Says Investor
content: Ross Gerber, President and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki, reacts to a rough earnings report as revenue for the EV maker misses estimates.  Tesla has felt the impact of founder Elon Musk's political entanglements, leading to a sales slump. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tesla's Success Comes From Musk's Vision: Former Tesla Executive
content: Karim Bousta, DVx Ventures Co-Founder and Former Tesla Executive, says Tesla is now behind in many aspects. Its new business model and car manufacturing, doing both at the same time, pose a major challenge for the company. He speaks with Scarlet Fu and Vonnie Quinn on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Alphabet Reports Strong Quarter, Boosts 2025 Capital Spending
content: Brent Thill, Jefferies senior technology research analyst, and Bloomberg's Mandeep Singh break down Alphabet's 2nd quarter earnings as the tech giant reported strong sales and boosted capex. However, some concerns persist as Google tries to stay in the AI race. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Getting Out of Catch-Up Made Key For Alphabet: MNTN CEO
content: Mark Douglas, MNTN CEO, says Google has to transition the entire company to AI solutions, and it has to do so flawlessly. Douglas adds that AI-Powered ads are a major risk, and Google is showing it's willing to do whatever it takes to figure it out; he speaks to Scarlet Fu and Vonnie Quinn on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Modi Arrives in UK to Sign Trade Deal
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in London Wednesday where he's set to sign a landmark free trade agreement between India and the UK.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bank of America to Buy Back $40 Billion of Shares in New Program
content: Bank of America Corp. announced a new $40 billion stock-buyback program, sending shares up.

title: GoPro, Krispy Kreme Gain as Markets Abuzz About Meme Stocks
content: The meme-stock revival stretched into another day, even as an early-morning surge in shares of GoPro Inc., Krispy Kreme Inc. and Beyond Meat Inc. subsided by the close.

title: First Nations Oppose Possible British Columbia Oil Pipeline
content: A First Nations group in British Columbia sent an open letter to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urging him reject any proposal for a pipeline or oil tanker project in the northwest area of the province.

title: Tesla's Business Is in Decline, Says Ross Gerber
content: Ross Gerber, Gerber Kawasaki Wealth and Investment Management co-founder, president and CEO, says it's sad, but Tesla's business is in decline. Tesla's second-earnings missed expectations and revenue fell 12% to $22.5 billion. He speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Philippines Will Seek to Lower US Tariff to 15%, Envoy Says
content: The Philippines will aim to bring down the tariff imposed by the US on Philippine exports to 15% from 19%, Manila’s envoy to Washington said, as the Aug. 1 deadline set by President Donald Trump nears.

title: Blue States Score New Win Against Trump Birth Citizenship Ban
content: A federal appeals court in San Francisco ruled that President Donald Trump’s limits on birthright citizenship are unconstitutional in the latest setback for his immigration crackdown.

title: Columbia Agrees to $200 Million Fine to Settle White House Fight
content: Columbia University reached a landmark deal with the Trump administration to restore federal funding for research, easing a crisis that has rattled the school’s finances and upended its leadership.

title: South Korea Weighs US Investment Pledge to Trim Auto Tariff
content: The US and South Korea have discussed creating a fund to invest in American projects as part of a trade deal, similar to an agreement Japan struck Tuesday with President Donald Trump, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Trump’s DOJ Sidesteps Norms to Boost Ally Alina Habba as US Attorney
content: President Donald Trump’s administration sidestepped tradition this week and criticized judges who sought to bypass his ally as the top federal prosecutor in New Jersey — a pattern that may repeat itself in other Democratic-leaning states.

title: Thailand Recalls Ambassador From Cambodia as Border Conflict Deepens
content: Thailand recalled its envoy from Phnom Penh and expelled the Cambodian ambassador following a new landmine explosion that injured five Thai soldiers, marking the latest escalation in a simmering border dispute.

title: Saudi-Syrian Pacts Will Amount to $6 Billion, Minister Says
content: A Saudi-Syrian investment forum in Damascus will include the signing of 44 pacts worth about $6 billion, said Syria’s Information Minister Hamza al-Mustafa, as the war-ravaged country tries to revitalize its devastated economy through cooperation with the Gulf kingdom.

title: Milei’s Inner Circle See Cracks Emerge Over Ruling Party Hopefuls
content: The influential sister of Argentine President Javier Milei is trying to quash dissent within the ruling party that threatens to complicate the libertarian leader’s prospects in a pair of crucial upcoming elections.

title: US Agencies Open Debate on How to Define Ultra-Processed Foods
content: Three US agencies on Wednesday announced plans to formally open debate over how to define the term “ultra-processed” food, which is sure to prompt fierce lobbying from companies eager to exempt their products from the distinction.

title: Trump Weighed Nvidia Breakup But Was Told It Would Be ‘Hard’
content: President Donald Trump said he considered attempting to break up Nvidia Corp. to increase competition in artificial intelligence chips before finding out “it’s not easy in that business.”

title: Australia to Lift Import Curbs on US Beef to Pacify Trump
content: Australia intends to remove restrictions on US beef imports in a bid to appease President Donald Trump, who had highlighted Canberra’s biosecurity measures as an unfair impediment to trade.

title: Trump Signs AI Orders, Vows US Will Win Race Over New Technology
content: President Donald Trump signed executive orders to put in motion a new White House plan to boost artificial intelligence development in the US by loosening regulations and expanding energy supplies for data centers.

title: Sanctions, on Rise, Are as Deadly as Armed Conflict, Study Says
content: Sanctions can cause as many fatalities as armed conflict, with unilateral penalties being associated with more than half a million deaths per year, according to a new analysis.

title: House Subpoenas Maxwell as WSJ Reports Trump in Epstein Files
content: A Republican-led House committee subpoenaed convicted sex offender and Jeffrey Epstein accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell on Wednesday to testify next month while the Wall Street Journal separately published its latest piece drawing a link between President Donald Trump and the disgraced financier.

title: Trump Says Countries Will Face Tariffs Ranging From 15% to 50%
content: US President Donald Trump suggested that he would not go below 15% as he sets so-called reciprocal tariff rates ahead of an Aug. 1 deadline, an indication that the floor for the increased levies was rising.

title: UK Touts India Trade Deal Worth £4.8 Billion as Modi Jets In
content: The UK and India plan to sign their long-awaited free trade agreement on Thursday, in a move which the British government said would add £4.8 billion ($6.5 billion) to the size of the economy.

title: Zelenskiy Risks Ukraine EU Bid as Protest Over Graft Office Grow
content: Protests flared across Ukraine for the second night after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy’s decision to hobble anti-corruption authorities. The move blindsided Kyiv’s allies and may have inflicted lasting damage to its ambition to join the European Union.

title: Xi to Meet EU Chiefs at Downsized Summit Hit by Trade, Ukraine
content: Top representatives from the European Union will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and other key leaders Thursday, their first in-person summit since 2023 that’s exposing a divide between the bloc and Beijing just months after earlier signs of a possible detente.

title: Supreme Court Lets Trump Oust Top Consumer-Safety Officials
content: A divided US Supreme Court let President Donald Trump temporarily remove three Democratic members of the Consumer Product Safety Commission, extending a line of decisions giving the White House more control over independent agencies.

title: Trump’s Japan Trade Deal Raises Fears He Gave Away Too Much
content: US industries and protectionists are raising alarms with President Donald Trump’s pact with Japan, saying it risks undercutting his stated goals of rebalancing America’s trading relationships and reviving domestic manufacturing.

title: Speaker Johnson Bets Early Trump Tax Cuts to Help GOP Hold House in 2026
content: House Speaker Mike Johnson is betting the upfront rewards from President Donald Trump’s tax law will carry his party in the 2026 midterm elections, allowing Republicans to defy US political convention and hold on to their House majority.

title: Russia-Ukraine Talks End With Deal on POWs, No Progress on Peace
content: Officials from Russia and Ukraine ended a third round of formal negotiations in Istanbul with an agreement to swap more prisoners but little sign of progress on a deal to halt the war.

title: Justice Department Prepares Crackdown on Trump Tariff Violators
content: Federal prosecutors are laying the groundwork to criminally charge companies and individuals that try to evade US tariffs as President Donald Trump readies a fresh round of levies next week.

title: Trump’s AI Plan Urges Lighter Touch by FTC in Win for Microsoft
content: Microsoft Corp. stands to gain from new White House AI guidelines that call on the US Federal Trade Commission to show more restraint in probes involving artificial intelligence and stand down on cases that put “AI innovation” at risk.

title: Ecuador Indigenous Union Vote Eases Anti-Government Stance
content: Ecuador’s Indigenous union, CONAIE, is softening its confrontational stance following bursts of violent anti-government protests that diminished the group’s political relevance.

title: Iran May Still Withdraw From Nuclear Treaty, Negotiator Says
content: Iran has “not ruled out” withdrawing from the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons if the United Nations were to reimpose sanctions, a lead Iranian negotiator said ahead of nuclear talks this week.

content: The Adani Group has shelved its plans to build a consumer-facing super app after incurring significant losses and internal turmoil, people familiar with the matter said, marking a retreat from its ambitions to build “the Ferrari of the digital world.”

title: Microsoft Hack Hits Hundreds of Firms, Agencies as Damage Spreads
content: The number of companies and organizations compromised by a security vulnerability in Microsoft Corp.’s SharePoint servers is increasing rapidly, with the tally of victims soaring more than six-fold in a few days, according to one research firm.

title: SK Hynix Quickens AI Investments After Posting Record Profit
content: SK Hynix Inc. outlined plans to speed up spending on advanced memory chip production capacity after reporting record earnings, reflecting surging AI demand.

title: Alphabet Boosted by AI, Cloud Demand as Spending Needs Skyrocket
content: Alphabet Inc. said demand for artificial intelligence products boosted quarterly sales, and now requires an extreme increase in capital spending — heightening pressure on the company to justify the cost of keeping up in the AI race.

title: Musk Puts Potential xAI Investment Back on Tesla Shareholders
content: Elon Musk suggested any potential investment by Tesla Inc. in his artificial intelligence startup, xAI, should be proposed by the electric carmaker’s shareholders.

title: Walmart Hires Instacart Executive to Speed Up AI Adoption
content: Walmart Inc. is hiring an executive from Instacart Inc. to accelerate its use of artificial intelligence as the world’s largest retailer looks to bolster its competitive edge.

title: Pritzker Lures Another Startup for Chicago’s Quantum Campus
content: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker has sealed a deal to bring another company to his Chicago quantum computing campus after investments from PsiQuantum Corp. and International Business Machines Corp.

title: AMD CEO Sees Chips From TSMC’s US Plant Costing 5%-20% More
content: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. Chief Executive Officer Lisa Su said that the chips her company gets from supplier Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. cost more when they’re produced in TSMC’s Arizona facilities.

content: International Business Machines Corp. reported weaker-than-expected sales in its closely watched software segment, disappointing investors who have grown increasingly optimistic about the business.

title: T-Mobile Beats Estimates for Phone Sign-Ups, Lifts Guidance
content: T-Mobile US Inc., the nation’s second-largest wireless provider, reported more new subscribers than analysts were expecting in the second quarter, overcoming a sluggish start to the year.

content: Bloomberg’s Caroline Hyde and Ed Ludlow discuss the newly released US AI Action Plan, which centers on open-source development and aims to expand national data center capacity. And, Tesla, Alphabet, and IBM are among the companies releasing earnings after markets close. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ServiceNow Gives Strong Revenue Outlook, Touts AI Sales
content: ServiceNow Inc. gave a strong outlook for revenue growth and touted customer adoption of its artificial intelligence software tools.

content: NIQ Global Intelligence Plc shares slumped 9.5% after the company raised $1.05 billion in an initial public offering.

title: Fiserv Shares’ Slump Worsens as Merchant Growth Misses
content: Fiserv Inc.’s stock plunged Wednesday after the financial-technology company reported lackluster growth in its merchant business.

title: PDD Analysts See HK Listing as More Likely After Auditor Change
content: PDD Holdings Inc.’s move to switch to a Hong Kong-based auditor may indicate the Chinese e-commerce firm is preparing to apply for a second listing there, according to two analysts.

title: Jack Dorsey’s Mainstream Dream Faces Test as Block Joins S&P 500
content: Jack Dorsey’s Block Inc. joins the coveted S&P 500 on Wednesday, a symbolic milestone that puts the digital finance firm — pursuing everything from mobile banking to Bitcoin mining — under Wall Street’s spotlight.

title: AT&T Deals Deliver Surge in Second-Quarter Phone Customers
content: AT&T Inc. reported second-quarter results that mostly exceeded Wall Street estimates, including faster-than-expected growth in wireless phone subscribers after offering perks and incentives to attract customers from rivals.

title: Texas Instruments Suffers Worst Rout Since ’08 on Tepid Forecast
content: Texas Instruments Inc., a key chipmaker for producers of cars and factory equipment, suffered the worst stock decline in 17 years after stoking fears that a tariff-fueled sales surge will be short-lived.

title: Digicel Launches $2.7 Billion Junk-Debt Offering for Refinancing
content: Digicel Group Holdings Ltd. kicked off a $2.7 billion junk-debt sale as it looks to refinance bonds and loans coming due in the next few years.

title: Rogers Hikes Revenue Forecast After Toronto Sports Deal
content: Rogers Communications Inc. beat analysts’ estimates in the second quarter, posting higher sales in its wireless and media divisions, and raised its 2025 revenue outlook after buying control of Toronto’s basketball and hockey teams.

title: Nintendo Switch 2 Sets Record as Fastest-Selling Console in US
content: Nintendo Co.’s new Switch 2 console sustained its blistering start to sales globally by setting a new record for the fastest-selling video game device in US history.

title: Hedge Fund Waratah Breach Said to Have Exposed Client Data
content: Waratah Capital Advisors Ltd., a Canadian hedge fund, is investigating a cybersecurity breach that may have exposed sensitive client information, including names, social insurance numbers and account balances, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Nuclear Weapons Agency Breached in Microsoft SharePoint Hack
content: The US agency responsible for maintaining and designing the nation’s cache of nuclear weapons was among those breached by a hack of Microsoft Corp.’s SharePoint document management software, according to a person with knowledge of the matter.

title: SAP Says Trade War, Dollar Weakness Weighing on Bottom Line
content: SAP SE warned that the global trade war and the dollar’s weakness are weighing on its business. Shares of the German software company fell.

title: AI Boom Leads to Record US Grid Costs, Call for New Plants
content: Businesses and households served by the largest US power grid will spend a record $16.1 billion to ensure electricity supplies amid a massive artificial intelligence-driven demand surge.

title: RBA Finds Foreign Students Add to Australia’s Housing Demand
content: International students in Australia exert more pressure on demand in the economy, including in the housing market, rather than adding to supply, according to a new Reserve Bank analysis.

title: Korea’s Economy Posts Rebound Amid Tariff, Property Risks
content: South Korea’s economy returned to growth last quarter after a modest contraction in the previous period, signaling resilience even as trade tensions simmer and domestic financial risks deepen.

title: RBNZ Chair Says Orr ‘Lost His Cool’ With Treasury Officials
content: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Chair Neil Quigley apologized to a Treasury Department official for the behavior of Governor Adrian Orr less than two weeks before Orr abruptly quit.

title: Hungary’s GKI Business Confidence Index Plunges to Five-Year Low
content: Hungary’s business confidence index plunged to its lowest level in almost five years, in another sign that the economy could be on the brink of another recession.

title: BOJ Watchers Still Predict Next Rate Hike in October or January
content: Bank of Japan watchers increasingly expect authorities to raise the benchmark interest rate either in October or January, according to a Bloomberg survey conducted before US President Donald Trump announced a trade deal with Japan.

title: EU Sees Progress Toward US Trade Deal With 15% Tariffs
content: The European Union and the US are progressing toward an agreement that would set a 15% tariff for most imports, according to diplomats briefed on the negotiations.

title: Speaker Johnson Says He’s Become ‘Disenchanted’ With Powell
content: House Speaker Mike Johnson said he is “disenchanted” with Jerome Powell, as President Donald Trump attacks the Federal Reserve chairman over frustrations with high interest rates.

title: Malawi Faces $2 Billion Reserves Hole This Year, IMF Says
content: Malawi’s net international reserves will plunge $2 billion into negative territory in 2025, according to the International Monetary Fund — an amount that’s equivalent to almost a fifth of the nation’s total economy.

title: Chicago CFO Expects Property Tax Hike in Next Budget Package
content: Chicago’s Chief Financial Officer Jill Jaworski said the city will likely seek to raise property taxes to address next year’s budget deficit.

title: Johnson Kicks Off Next Tax Bill Work, Seeking Fall Passage
content: House Republicans are starting work on a follow-up to their recently enacted tax-and-spending law, aiming to pass provisions that were removed from President Donald Trump’s “one big, beautiful bill,” Speaker Mike Johnson said in an interview Wednesday with Bloomberg Government.

title: US Existing-Home Sales Fall to Nine-Month Low on Record Prices
content: Sales of previously owned US homes fell in June to a nine-month low as potential buyers continued to bristle at record prices and high borrowing costs.

title: Nigeria Collects More Than Half Targeted 2025 Tax in Six Months
content: Nigeria collected more than half its targeted annual tax revenue in the first six months of the year, despite the oil price dropping below budget projections.

title: EU and China Intend to Sign Climate Statement at Beijing Summit
content: The European Union and China are preparing a landmark joint statement on climate cooperation, a move that could help galvanize momentum ahead of the COP30 summit in Brazil later this year.

title: Kenya’s Revenue Raising Seen Constrained Until After 2027 Vote
content: Kenyan authorities will struggle to introduce revenue-raising measures before 2027 elections, constraining the government’s attempts to narrow the budget-financing gap, according to Moody’s Ratings.

title: Bessent Says ‘No Rush’ to Choose Successor to Fed’s Powell
content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that there’s “no rush” to identify a successor to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, and that a nominee could potentially come from current board members or the heads of the district banks.

title: Luxury Boom in Milei’s Argentina Masks Despair Among the Masses
content: A boom in homes, cars and flights contrasts with empty shops and restaurants.

title: US Tariffs Are Changing Europe’s Approach to Chinese Investment
content: China is pivoting to higher-value investments in Hungary, Slovakia and other nations within its growing orbit.

title: India’s RBI Says Growth Boosted by Agriculture, Services
content: India’s economy remained largely resilient despite global uncertainties, due to a robust agricultural season, strong momentum in the services sector and modest industrial growth, the Reserve Bank of India said in its monthly bulletin.

title: Turkey Poised For First Rate Cut Since Political Crisis in March
content: Turkey’s central bank is expected to make its first interest-rate cut since a political crisis in March, which caused policymakers to reverse an easing cycle.

title: Zimbabwe Says Informal Sector Dominates 76% of the Economy
content: Zimbabwe estimates that more than three-quarters of economic activity takes place in the informal sector, depriving the government of much-needed tax revenue, according to the findings of its first economic census.

title: South Africa Lawmakers Back Schedule to Process Budget
content: South African lawmakers will spend the coming weeks processing Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s third draft of the national budget after a dispute within the coalition government over taxes saw two previous versions scrapped.

title: Asia Comes to Grips With the New US Tariff Landscape
content: I’m Malcolm Scott, international economics enterprise editor in Sydney. Today we’re looking at what the latest US tariff deals mean for Asia. Send us feedback and tips to ecodaily@bloomberg.net. And if you aren’t yet signed up to receive this newsletter, you can do so here.

title: Asia’s Trump Tariff Rates Are Coming Into Force Lower Than Threatened
content: President Donald Trump’s latest tariff deals are starting to offer businesses some clarity after months of blinding uncertainty.

title: DOGE Cuts Risk Bogging Down Push to Implement Trump’s Tax Breaks
content: Staffing shortfalls and intricate new policies are complicating efforts at the Treasury Department and IRS to meet President Donald Trump’s tight deadlines for churning out guidance on his multi-trillion-dollar tax bill.

title: Defiant Ishiba Seeks to Prolong Premiership After US-Japan Deal
content: Embattled Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba denied media reports that he is set to announce his resignation, in an apparent bid to extend his premiership despite an election setback earlier in the week.

title: South Africa to Amend Budget Process After Political Wrangling
content: South Africa’s National Treasury plans to revamp its 2026 budget-preparation process after political wrangling saw this year’s proposal altered twice.

title: Macquarie Abruptly Replaces CFO Harvey as Bank Faces Probes
content: Macquarie Group Ltd.’s Alex Harvey will step down as chief financial officer, abruptly ending his almost three-decade career despite being seen as a contender to lead the Australian giant that’s beset by regulatory probes.

title: Musk Warns of ‘Rough’ Patch After Tesla’s Difficult Quarter
content: Elon Musk warned of a hard year ahead for Tesla Inc., adding to the automaker’s woes after reporting one of its worst quarters of the last decade.

title: China’s Chery to Supply Tech to Help India’s JSW Launch Own EVs
content: China’s Chery Automobile Co. will supply technology and components to billionaire Sajjan Jindal’s JSW Group to help launch a new-energy vehicle brand in India by 2027, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Chipotle Cuts Outlook on Traffic Slump Despite Free Burritos
content: Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. shares plunged after cutting its annual outlook for the second time this year, suggesting that honey chicken and burrito giveaways haven’t been enough to offset a traffic slump that the company attributed to economic anxiety.

title: Tesla Warns of Pain From Trump’s Tax Bill That Elon Musk Blasted
content: Tesla Inc. warned that provisions in President Donald Trump’s $3.4 trillion fiscal package will pose meaningful challenges for the EV maker in the next several months.

title: Southwest Air Cuts $1 Billion From Outlook on Tariff Fallout
content: Southwest Airlines Co. expects economic turmoil to erase as much as $1 billion of its annual pre-tax profit this year, prompting the US airline to offer shareholders a much-reduced outlook for 2025.

title: The Unexplained 10 Seconds Before the Deadly Air India Crash
content: What was happening during those moments in the cockpit as the Boeing Dreamliner rapidly lost altitude may hold the key to unlocking the tragedy.

content: That’s a wrap. Here are my key takeaways from Tesla’s second-quarter earnings:

title: CSX CEO Is Open to ‘All Possibilities’ as Rivals Look for Deals
content: CSX Corp. Chief Executive Officer Joe Hinrichs said he’s open to merger talks with other companies amid reports that Union Pacific Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp. are discussing a combination.

title: Mattel Reissues Forecast, Says Stores’ Slow Orders Cut Sales
content: Mattel Inc. introduced a new forecast for 2025 sales and profit — two months after pulling its previous outlook over the uncertainty tied to President Donald Trump’s tariff policies.

title: Neuralink Sees $1 Billion of Revenue by 2031 in Vast Expansion
content: Elon Musk’s brain implant company Neuralink Corp. expects to put its chips in 20,000 people a year by 2031, generating at least $1 billion in annual revenue, in a major ramp up of its work to treat disease and gain unprecedented access to the human mind, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg.

title: Sarepta Needs to Show FDA Elevidys Won’t Cause More Deaths
content: The Food and Drug Administration won’t sign off on Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. bringing its controversial gene therapy back to the market until the company can persuade US regulators that it won’t cause more deaths, according to an official familiar with the situation.

title: SEC Clears CSX After Investigating Old Accounting Errors
content: The US Securities and Exchange Commission dropped its probe of CSX Corp.’s previously reported accounting errors and certain non-financial metrics, the company disclosed on Wednesday.

title: Edison Sets Up Compensation Program for Eaton Fire Victims
content: Southern California Edison will set up a program to compensate victims of a deadly Los Angeles wildfire that it has acknowledged may be linked to the company’s electrical equipment.

title: Alberto Safra’s ASA Is Cutting Some Jobs After Gauss Acquisition
content: Billionaire Alberto Safra’s investment firm, ASA, is dismissing about 10 employees, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Judges Order Abrego Garcia’s Release, Bar New Arrest by ICE
content: Embattled Salvadoran immigrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia scored a pair of wins against the Trump administration as judges in two states issued rulings supporting his freedom while he fights federal human smuggling charges.

title: Tesla in Talks With Nevada as It Explores Robotaxi Expansion
content: Tesla Inc. is in early talks with officials in Nevada to establish autonomous vehicle operations in the state as the automaker plans an expansion of its recently introduced robotaxi service.

title: Fenway Park Workers Plan Strike Ahead of Three Red Sox Games
content: About 1,000 workers who staff concession stands at Fenway Park baseball stadium — the iconic home of the Boston Red Sox — and the MGM Music hall next door are planning to strike Friday after negotiations between their union and food service company Aramark failed.

title: Hasbro Sales Beat Estimates Thanks to ‘Magic’ Cards Surge
content: Hasbro Inc. raised its full-year outlook after a record quarter for its Magic: The Gathering card game. The company also reported revenue and earnings that beat analysts’ expectations.

title: TD Orders Staff Back to Office Four Days a Week Later This Year
content: Toronto-Dominion Bank became the latest Canadian bank to inform employees on hybrid work arrangements they’ll be expected in the office four days a week later this year, according to an internal memo.

title: America Movil Sees Service Revenue Growth Across Geographies
content: Billionaire Carlos Slim’s wireless provider America Movil SAB saw its service revenue grow 7.3% in the second quarter year over year, a sign it’s starting to benefit from a strengthening Mexico economy.

title: Northern Trust Shares Fall After CEO Dismisses Talk of Takeover
content: Northern Trust Corp. shares fell as much as 6% after the bank’s management dismissed recent reports of takeover talks and said it doesn’t intend to sell the company.

title: Walgreens Boots Launches Bond Tender After Sycamore Buyout Deal
content: Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. is launching a multi-currency debt tender, marking the latest step in its capital restructuring after banks offloaded a $4.5 billion debt package to help finance Sycamore Partners’ buyout of the Boots pharmacy chain.

title: Televisa Shares Rise on Improvements to Its Cable Operations
content: Grupo Televisa SAB shares rose after the company reported higher profits than analysts expected as improvements to its cable operations helped reduce churn.
